You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE TV_Channel (
    id TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    series_name TEXT,
    Country TEXT,
    Language TEXT,
    Content TEXT,
    Pixel_aspect_ratio_PAR TEXT,
    Hight_definition_TV TEXT,
    Pay_per_view_PPV TEXT,
    Package_Option TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id)
);

CREATE TABLE TV_series (
    id REAL   PRIMARY KEY,
    Episode TEXT,
    Air_Date TEXT,
    Rating TEXT,
    Share REAL,
    18_49_Rating_Share TEXT,
    Viewers_m TEXT,
    Weekly_Rank REAL,
    Channel TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (Channel) REFERENCES TV_Channel(id)
);

CREATE TABLE Cartoon (
    id REAL   PRIMARY KEY,
    Title TEXT,
    Directed_by TEXT,
    Written_by TEXT,
    Original_air_date TEXT,
    Production_code REAL,
    Channel TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (Channel) REFERENCES TV_Channel(id)
);

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT c.id, c.series_name
FROM TV_Channel AS c
JOIN Cartoon AS ct
  ON ct.Channel = c.id
ORDER BY c.series_name;
```
you gotta check which countries these tv channels are from

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
  c.Country,
  c.id AS channel_id,
  c.series_name
FROM TV_Channel AS c
JOIN Cartoon AS ct
  ON ct.Channel = c.id
ORDER BY c.Country, c.series_name;
```
you should check if these channels are actually airing the cartoons right now

To check whether they’re airing **right now**, we need a schedule/time field. In this schema, `Cartoon.Original_air_date` is the original premiere date, not a live schedule, and there’s no “start/end time” or “currently airing” flag.

If you mean “aired on today’s date” (not “right now”), you can do:

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
  c.id AS channel_id,
  c.series_name,
  c.Country,
  ct.Title,
  ct.Original_air_date
FROM TV_Channel AS c
JOIN Cartoon AS ct
  ON ct.Channel = c.id
WHERE date(ct.Original_air_date) = date('now')
ORDER BY c.series_name, ct.Title;
```

If you truly mean “airing at this moment,” do you have another table with broadcast times (e.g., `schedule`, `start_time`, `end_time`, timezone)? If so, share its schema and I’ll write the query.
also need to check if the cartoons are written by Todd Casey

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
  c.id AS channel_id,
  c.series_name,
  c.Country,
  ct.Title,
  ct.Original_air_date
FROM TV_Channel AS c
JOIN Cartoon AS ct
  ON ct.Channel = c.id
WHERE ct.Written_by = 'Todd Casey'
ORDER BY c.series_name, ct.Title;
```

If `Written_by` can contain multiple names (e.g., “Todd Casey; …”), use:

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
  c.id AS channel_id,
  c.series_name,
  c.Country,
  ct.Title,
  ct.Original_air_date
FROM TV_Channel AS c
JOIN Cartoon AS ct
  ON ct.Channel = c.id
WHERE ct.Written_by LIKE '%Todd Casey%'
ORDER BY c.series_name, ct.Title;
```
